fingerprint.reproducibility_note: Identical bytecode alone does not guarantee identical results. Reproduction requires the same analyzer version, rule-set version, EVM revision and configuration. Symbolic results can also differ if the wall-clock budget (max_seconds) or Z3 timeouts are hit at different points.

REENT-001.title: State update reachable after external CALL
REENT-001.description: A CALL instruction is followed, on at least one resolved CFG path, by an SSTORE. If the callee can re-enter before the SSTORE executes, state read before the call may be stale.
preconditions: Callee is attacker-controlled or can call back into this contract.
State written after the call influences a check performed before it.
false_positives: Reentrancy guard implemented via storage lock set before the call.
Callee is a fixed trusted contract or a precompile.
Post-call SSTORE is unrelated to any pre-call check (e.g. event counters).
Call target is the contract itself or a view-only helper.
limitations: Only CALL is considered; CALLCODE/DELEGATECALL/STATICCALL are listed in coverage, not analysed.
CFG omits edges through unresolved dynamic jumps; SSTOREs behind them are not seen (false negatives).
Storage slots are compared only when both are compile-time constants within one basic block.
Cross-function and cross-contract reentrancy are not modelled.
Call value is classified only when its value is a visible constant within the block.

findings.title: State update after external call (potential reentrancy)
findings.description: The CALL at 0xf1 can be followed on a resolved control-flow path by 1 SSTORE instruction(s). If the callee re-enters before the write, checks made on earlier state may be bypassed.
preconditions: Callee is attacker-controlled or can call back into this contract.
State written after the call influences a check performed before it.
remediation: Apply checks-effects-interactions: perform storage updates before the external call.
Or use a reentrancy guard (non-reentrant lock) on state-changing entry points.
Prefer pull-payment patterns for value transfers.
verification_steps: Map the offsets to source via the compiler's source map / your build artifacts.
Write a test with a malicious callee that re-enters before the SSTORE executes.
Re-run the analysis on the patched bytecode and review the evidence manually; absence of a finding is not proof of a fix.
false_positive_considerations: Reentrancy guard implemented via storage lock set before the call.
Callee is a fixed trusted contract or a precompile.
Post-call SSTORE is unrelated to any pre-call check (e.g. event counters).
Call target is the contract itself or a view-only helper.
limitations: Only CALL is considered; CALLCODE/DELEGATECALL/STATICCALL are listed in coverage, not analysed.
CFG omits edges through unresolved dynamic jumps; SSTOREs behind them are not seen (false negatives).
Storage slots are compared only when both are compile-time constants within one basic block.
Cross-function and cross-contract reentrancy are not modelled.
Call value is classified only when its value is a visible constant within the block.
5 unresolved dynamic jump(s) exist; the CFG is incomplete.
findings.potential_impact: If exploitable: repeated withdrawals or violated accounting invariants. Exploitability is NOT assessed by this rule.

assumptions: Execution starts at offset 0 with an empty stack and zeroed memory; storage, calldata, caller, value and block environment are unconstrained symbols (caller/address/origin are < 2^160, calldatasize < 2^32).
CALL/STATICCALL return an unconstrained success flag. Callee behaviour is NOT modelled: no reentrancy into this contract, no balance changes, no returndata, no memory write to the return area.
LOG0-LOG4 are treated as side-effect-free. GAS and MSIZE return fresh unconstrained values.
KECCAK256 over a concrete length <= 256 is an uninterpreted function of the hashed bytes (no collision-resistance or real-hash facts are modelled).
BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODEHASH, BLOCKHASH, BLOBHASH are uninterpreted functions of their argument.

limitations: Results are limited to the rules and EVM subset listed in this report; absence of findings does NOT mean the contract is secure.
Only REENT-001 (state write after CALL) is implemented. Other vulnerability classes are not analysed.
No source code is available or inferred; offsets refer to the supplied runtime bytecode.
Trailing compiler metadata (e.g. Solidity CBOR) is decoded as instructions and may appear as unknown opcodes.
Control flow is reconstructed only from intra-block constant jump targets; dynamic jumps are unresolved.
